summary.headline: Salzer Q4 FY26 revenue rose 26% YoY to INR 474 crore, but margins fell to 7% on petrochemical and copper cost pressure; FY27 EBITDA guidance is 9-9.5%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR 474 crore, with EBITDA excluding other income of INR 31 crore (7% margin) and PAT of INR 10 crore. FY26 revenue rose 24% to INR 1,758 crore, but EBITDA margin was about 8% and PAT grew only 3% to INR 54 crore. Management attributed the margin squeeze to plastic (petrochemical-linked) cost increases of 2-3% of margin, copper and silver increases, freight and Middle East disruption. Working capital reached about 30% of revenue against a stated 25% ceiling, and management guided to a return to 25% in FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Kaycee Industries FY26 revenue / EBITDA / PAT
financial_highlights.value: INR 60 crore / INR 8 crore / INR 5 crore

segments.name: Industrial switchgear
segments.commentary: 56% of FY26 revenue and 51% of Q4; grew 20% YoY in FY26 and 15% in Q4. EBITDA margin 11% in FY26 and 8% in Q4; management says switchgear gross margin is about 35-40%.

segments.name: Wires and cables
segments.commentary: About 39% of FY26 revenue and 43% of Q4; grew 30% YoY in FY26 and 42% in Q4. EBITDA margin 5% in FY26 and 4% in Q4, with nearly all sales B2B.

segments.name: Building products
segments.commentary: About 5% of FY26 revenue and 6% of Q4; grew 16% YoY in FY26 and 36% in Q4.

segments.name: EV charging (Ultrafast Chargers, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: About 100 chargers sold, generating roughly INR 9 crore revenue to date; orders for close to 100 DC fast chargers held. Currently break-even at low volumes, targeted 12-15% EBITDA margin at scale; FY27 revenue expected around INR 25 crore.

segments.name: Smart metering
segments.commentary: About INR 45 crore of business executed over the last year; no large long-term orders secured yet. Addressable market about 17 crore meters, with AMISP requirements of 2-3 crore meters under discussion. No FY27 smart meter guidance given.

segments.name: Energy management (Effilume SPV)
segments.commentary: INR 200 crore Bangalore Corporation street-lighting automation project under execution; revenue expected to start in Q2 FY27 at a steady monthly run rate.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 9-9.5% for the full year (management clarified 'whole year' rather than exit rate); earlier guidance of 9.5-10% has been pushed out.
Margins expected to be under pressure in Q1 FY27 and stabilise from Q2 FY27; switchgear EBITDA margin expected at 12-13% from Q2 onwards.
Existing-business revenue expected at INR 2,000-2,100 crore in FY27, excluding smart meter upside.
June 2026 price increase of 7-10% across products, after a roughly 15% increase in February 2026; management expects 100% cost pass-through over the two increases.
Exports targeted at about 25% of FY27 revenue; Middle East and Africa exports of about INR 24 crore expected to double over FY27-28.
Interest cost expected to rise at least 10% in FY27 on higher working capital; depreciation flat. Average short-term borrowing cost about 8%.
Working capital to return to 25% or below of revenue in FY27; target ROCE of about 18%, with management implying 18-20% by FY30.
capex_capacity: Saudi Arabia manufacturing plant delayed about six months by the Middle East conflict from February 2026; capital equipment ordered, expected by August 2026, with operations from September or October 2026.
Saudi Phase-1 investment about INR 15 crore, with no capex escalation; Saudi plant targets about INR 100 crore revenue for GCC markets, starting with switchgear.
In-house fully integrated EMS facility installed for PCB assembly for smart meters.
Aurawin SPV formed with a smart-metering market participant to act as a bidding company for future tenders.
Management said it is not yet giving a smart meter guidance and expects some orders, but is holding inventory currently.
demand_pricing: Management expects Indian electrical equipment market to grow at double digits over the next four to five years, driven by electrification, data centres, renewables, EV charging and smart meter rollout.

Price increase in February 2026 of about 15% did not fully offset costs; plastic price increase in Q4 to be offset only with the June 2026 price increase. Market accepted the February increase smoothly, per management.

Exports grew about 5% YoY in FY26; US tariffs cut exports about 6% and Middle East crisis reduced business by around 10-12%. Americas and Europe together make up about half of exports. UK benefits from favourable currency and zero import duty.

Competitive position: management says Salzer is in the top three in most products on quality and pricing, and commands a premium in some categories; competitors include foreign, Chinese and other country players.
Largest client concentration is Schneider Electric at about 12% of revenue (includes business formerly with L&T).

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of the FY27 EBITDA margin guidance given recent price hikes and April volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance cut to 9-9.5% for FY27 (whole year). A further 7-10% price increase in June 2026 is planned; Q1 pressure expected, with margin stabilising in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the wires and cables EBITDA margin so low, and does the segment cover its interest cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly B2B (about 70% per the answer), and copper cost rise means a fixed absolute profit is now a lower percentage (margin was 6.5-7% a couple of years ago). Management said the business earns about 2-3% PAT after interest.

qa_highlights.question: Would management consider demerging wires and cables or other shareholder value unlocking steps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the suggestion was taken positively and would be looked at, with no commitment or timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Why has working capital and short-term debt risen, and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital reached about 30% of revenue versus a 25% ceiling, due to margin erosion, smart meter capex and slow scale-up. Management expects a return to 25% or below in FY27. Receivable days are 90-95 on net sales basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi plant business model and investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant aimed at local content requirements in Saudi projects; delayed about six months; Phase-1 capex about INR 15 crore; target INR 100 crore revenue for GCC.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the EV charging business margins and revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently break-even due to low volumes; target EBITDA 12-15% at scale; FY27 revenue expected about INR 25 crore.

risks_watch: Petrochemical-linked plastic and copper/silver costs; Q1 FY27 margins expected to remain under pressure before the June price increase takes effect.
Working capital and short-term borrowing (INR 503 crore) versus the 25% of revenue target; interest cost expected to rise at least 10% in FY27.
Smart meter execution remains slow, with no large long-term orders secured and inventory being held.
Middle East conflict affecting Saudi plant timeline and exports; US tariffs reducing export volumes.
Saudi plant commissioning (August-October 2026) and the INR 200 crore Bangalore project revenue starting in Q2 FY27.
Shareholder value concerns over low wires and cables returns and the possible demerger, which management has not committed to.
summary.management_tone: Management was candid about margin pressure, attributing it to external cost shocks and admitting earlier guidance was missed; it was confident on pricing pass-through and on long-term demand. It was non-committal on smart meter volumes, raw material breakdowns and any demerger or capital structure action.

Ideally, we want to pass on 100% of the increase to the customer.
We will definitely take your suggestion in a positive. We'll see what we can do on that.
